<details>
The PKGBUILD uses a standard source definition pointing to the official upstream GitHub repository (https://github.com/SylEleuth/gruvbox-plus-icon-pack). The `source=` line specifies a tarball URL from the project's own repository, which is the expected and normal behavior for AUR packages. 

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the build process is intentionally skipped:
- `--nobuild` prevents the build phase from running
- `--noprepare` prevents the prepare phase from running  
- The `package()` function only copies icon theme directories to the installation path and performs no code execution

These flags ensure that no code from the source archive is executed, and no untrusted payload is run. The only action taken is fetching the tarball from the upstream repository (which is allowed and expected for auditing purposes). According to the security guidelines, missing or SKIPped checksums are NOT grounds to fail this gate—the full PKGBUILD review will handle verification concerns separately. Standard source definitions from known upstream repositories are considered normal and safe.

There are no malicious commands (eval, base64, curl, wget, etc.), no top-level command substitution, and no unexpected file operations that could compromise the system. The file follows standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's GitHub repository using a versioned tarball over HTTPS. The source URL is constructed predictably from `pkgname`, `pkgver`, and the upstream `url`, pointing to a specific release archive (`v$pkgver.tar.gz`). The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, so the integrity of the downloaded source will be verified during extraction.

No command substitutions, function overrides, or executable logic appear in the global scope or within `pkgver()`. The `pkgver` variable is set statically as `6.6.0`, with a comment hint for a tool (renovate) to track GitHub tags — this is metadata and does not execute any code. There are no network requests, data exfiltrations, or dangerous operations performed during sourcing of the PKGBUILD.

Since `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only fetch and verify the source (using the provided hash) and parse the PKGBUILD without executing `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`, there is no risk of malicious code execution during this phase.
</details>
